_comment: RETRY of the force-AUX-default test. Earlier attempts wrote their package to a folder called SMEG_PLUS_UPG_auxdefault, and the updater only ever looks for the payload at the hard-coded '/bd0/SMEG_PLUS_UPG/NAV/USER_DATA', so those runs were skipped. `out` below therefore ends in a literal SMEG_PLUS_UPG inside a throwaway parent, and that parent's contents go at the root of the stick; run tools/preflight.py on the built folder before flashing, it fails loudly on that mistake. FLASHED 2026-09-14: the update ran and the application image is patched, but the USER_DATA half STILL did not apply even though the stick layout was verified correct afterwards - so the folder name was not the (only) cause, and no value of supervisor.Last_Source has been tested on a car yet. See docs/VERIFICATION.md.
_value: Last_Source = 7, which C_MGR_SRC's own scheduler-position enum calls POS_AUX. Runtime SPY evidence separates this from raw SrcId: tuner logged Last_Source=1, SrcId=0xbc00 and Sched_Pos=1. The scheduler at 0x016957ec restores a source by matching node+0x18 (Sched_Pos) against Last_Source; raw SrcId is node+0x04. See docs/AUX_CHAIN.md.
_beacon: clock.Time_Zone is moved from 16 to 0 purely as a did-it-apply signal. It is unrelated to AUX, harmless, and revertible from the settings menu. After the flash, open the clock settings and read the configured time zone: if it is no longer the one you had, the USER_DATA payload was applied, and a unit that still starts on radio then means the value 7 is wrong. If the time zone is untouched, the payload was skipped again and the source result means nothing either way. Read the time zone entry in the menu rather than the clock face - a GPS-slaved clock shows the right time regardless. Only one thing that could affect the source is changed here, so the result is interpretable in both directions. OUTCOME 2026-09-14: the time zone was unchanged, so the payload was skipped again and the boot-to-radio result says nothing about the value.
